subject: Questions about constrains in a three-group dataset

messages.subject: Questions about constrains in a three-group dataset
parts:
Dear Phil,

I'm fitting a Rasch model and a three-factor model to a three-group dataset, but when using the multipleGroup function, I'm having trouble choosing the right syntax(constrain, constrainB, invariance) and identifying problems with my codes.

The data-frame looks like this:

Items 2, 3, 12, 13-20 are gpcm items, the rest are dichotomous items.
The last eight items are four pairs with the same stem but different item format, 13 & 17, 14 & 18, 15 & 19, 16 & 20, the first one in each pair is presented as a two-step multiple choice question whereas the second one as essay question.
For the three-factor model, the factor structure is specified like this:
mod3 <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-20
+                   F2 = 1, 4-10
+                   F3 = 12-20' )
I'm doing this analysis because I want to (1) compare whether the unidimensional model or the three-factor model fits better, (2) check the factor loadings and difficulty parameters for the four pairs of same-stem items.

Here are the codes I used:
nmsmul <- colnames(all3group)
moduni <- mirt.model('F1=1-20
                     constrainB = （13,17), (14,18), (15,19), (16,20)')
typeuni <- c("Rasch", "gpcm", "gpcm", "Rasch", "Rasch", "Rasch", "Rasch", "Rasch", "Rasch", "Rasch", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm", "gpcm")
groupmul <- c(rep('bnu',96), rep('bit',96), rep('bju',124))
all3outuni1 <- multipleGroup(all3group, moduni, groupmul, itemtype = typeuni, invariance = c(nmsmul[1:12], 'free_means', 'free_var'))
all3out1 <- multipleGroup(all3group, mod3, groupmul, invariance = c(nmsmul[1:12], 'free_means', 'free_var'), method = "MCEM")

The multidimensional model did not converge; the unidimensional model did, and here's part of the results (it'd take too much space to paste all the results here):

It seems to recognize constrainB = ... as another factor, and the factor loadings of the first 12 common items are different across groups. Also there's the problem that the multidimensional model did not converge in the end. I guess there's something wrong with my codes, but since I'm new to IRT and R programming, it's hard for me to determine where the problem lies: did I set the anchor items and constrains right (are they suitable for my second purpose)? Was there something wrong with how I used the syntax constrain/constrainB/invariance? Or was it because the items are just problematic?

I hope I've managed to make my questions understandable. I'm sorry if my limited knowledge might cause you extra trouble in responding to my questions. I'd appreciate your advice so much. Thanks in advance!

Regards!
Erin

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Questions about constrains in a three-group dataset
parts:
Hi Erin,

I think the main issue here is that the syntax specifications are case sensitive. Hence, constrainB is not equivalent to CONSTRAINB. The former is interpreted by the package as a unique factor, while the latter is a reserved keyword. I think fixing that up first will greatly help you locate the issue in the code, and I'd be happy to help with the remainder of your analysis after some of the initial kinks are worked out. Apologies for the delayed reply.

Phil
